desc:
Count the distinct palindromes of length exactly 3 that occur in s as a subsequence (letters taken in order, not necessarily next to each other). A palindrome of length 3 has the form xyx. Two subsequences that read the same count only once, however many ways there are to pick their positions.

For example, "aabca" contains "aaa", "aba" and "aca", so the answer is 3. "adc" has none, so the answer is 0. "bbcbaba" gives 4 (bbb, bcb, bab, aba).
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: A three-letter palindrome is fully described by its outer letter x and its middle letter y. There are only 26 × 26 possibilities.
For a fixed outer letter x, which positions of x are the best to use as the two outer letters?
Use the first and the last occurrence of x. Every distinct letter that appears strictly between them is a valid middle letter, so add the number of distinct letters in that stretch.
editorial: Fix the outer letter x. A subsequence x y x exists exactly when some occurrence of y sits between two occurrences of x. Taking the first and the last occurrence of x gives the widest window, so xyx is a subsequence if and only if y occurs somewhere strictly inside that window.

So for each letter with at least two occurrences, the contribution is the number of distinct letters in s[first+1 .. last-1]. Summing over the 26 letters counts every distinct palindrome exactly once, because different (x, y) pairs are different strings.
Each letter costs one scan of at most n characters, so the total is O(26 · n) time with O(26) extra space.
